title: NormasTCU --- A Brazilian Portuguese IR Dataset and an Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge for Relevance Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2608.27746v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Portuguese Information Retrieval (IR) lacks public datasets, and relevance assessment for specialized collections remains costly. While Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly support relevance assessment, their reliability in non-English specialized domains remains unclear. We introduce NormasTCU (https://huggingface.co/datasets/LeandroRibeiro/NormasTCU), a Brazilian Portuguese IR dataset with 14,469 legal documents, 46 queries, and 3,048 human judgments over 812 query-document pairs. Using NormasTCU, we evaluated LLM-as-a-judge for relevance assessment by prompting three models with two prompt techniques to grade these pairs. We then compared the rankings of 15 IR systems derived from LLM-generated and human reference qrels. LLMs consistently showed a positive scoring bias (mean absolute error: 0.46--0.66 on a 0-2 scale). Furthermore, pair-level agreement with human judgments achieved only fair to moderate levels, with Cohen's kappa

translated_title: NormasTCU——一个巴西葡萄牙语信息检索数据集及对LLM作为裁判进行相关性评估的评测
translated_abstract: 葡萄牙语信息检索（IR）领域缺乏公开数据集，且针对专业文献集合的相关性评估成本依然高昂。尽管大语言模型（LLM）日益广泛地被用于支持相关性评估，但其在非英语专业领域的可靠性仍不明确。我们提出了NormasTCU（https://huggingface.co/datasets/LeandroRibeiro/NormasTCU），这是一个巴西葡萄牙语IR数据集，包含14,469份法律文件、46个查询，以及针对812个查询-文档对的3,048条人工相关性判断。利用NormasTCU，我们通过两种提示技术对三个模型进行提示来为这些查询-文档对评分，从而评估了LLM作为裁判进行相关性评估的效果。随后，我们比较了分别基于LLM生成和人工参考qrels得出的15个IR系统的排名。LLM始终表现出正向评分偏差（在0-2分制上平均绝对误差为0.46-0.66）。此外，LLM与人工判断在查询-文档对层面的一致性仅达到一般至中等水平（Cohen's kappa...）
tldr: 该论文发布了包含14,469份法律文件的巴西葡萄牙语法律领域IR数据集NormasTCU，并发现LLM作为相关性评估裁判存在正向评分偏差、与人工判断一致性仅为一般至中等水平，表明其在非英语专业领域的可靠性仍然不足。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces NormasTCU, a Brazilian Portuguese IR dataset of 14,469 legal documents, and shows that LLM-as-a-judge exhibits a consistent positive scoring bias and only fair-to-moderate agreement with human judgments, revealing limited reliability of LLMs for relevance assessment in non-English specialized domains.
